newsitem.title: JAPAN: THAILAND, IMF MAY AGREE PACKAGE THIS WEEK--SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: THAILAND, IMF MAY AGREE PACKAGE THIS WEEK--SOURCE.

text.p: It is possible that Thailand and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) may reach an agreement on a financial support package for Thailand this week, an international monetary source said in Tokyo on Thursday.
Such an agreement would be followed by a meeting in Tokyo as early as next week among the IMF and Asian nations to work out a financial support package for Thailand, the source said.
He added that the date of the meeting would depend on when Thailand and the IMF reached an agreement in their ongoing talks over an economic adjustment programme.
"If the IMF and Thailand reach a final agreement there may be a meeting in Tokyo as early as next week to discuss the international financial support package for Thailand," the source said.

He added that although the meeting would be in Tokyo it would be under the auspices of the IMF and would be participated by officials from Asian nations and from other international financial organisations besides the IMF.
He also said the total package given by Asian nations and international bodies was unlikely to exceed $15 billion.
He added that he had no knowledge of the amount of financial support planned by private commercial banks.
Thailand has said it was seeking $12-$15 billion in loans from foreign countries and the IMF to stabilise its economy.
The monetary source said he was not aware that $7 billion in financial support would be provided by the Export-Import Bank of Japan (Ex-Im Bank), as reported in the Japanese media.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Thursday that Japan decided to contribute a maximum of $7 billion in loans through the Ex-Im Bank to a $20 billion international support package for Thailand.
The source said the amount of Japan's financial support for the Thai package will not exceed that of the IMF, adding that it will probably all come in the form of loans from the Ex-Im Bank.
"The amount of Japanese support will not exceed that of the IMF... And it's hard to conceive of anything other than the Ex-Im Bank (as a source of loans for Japanese support)," he said.
